reference: Barnhart, Cynthia, et al. "Airline schedule planning: Accomplishments and opportunities." Manufacturing & Service Operations Management (2003).
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
A compact time-expanded fleet-flow planning problem has fleet types V, locations L, time periods T, feasible legs A={(i,t,j,h): i != j, h > t}, and sparse active legs A_active subset A. Parameters are capacity q_v, operating cost c_v, available fleet a_v, active-leg indicator delta[i,t,j,h], and passenger demand P[i,t,j,h] only on active legs. Integer variable NumPlanes[v,i,t,j,h] is the number of fleet units of type v assigned to feasible leg (i,t,j,h). Integer variable NumIdlePlanes[v,i,t] tracks idle fleet at location i after the period-t balance, and NumIdlePlanesInit[v,i] is initial fleet placed at location i. Minimize sum_v,sum_a c_v NumPlanes[v,a]. Initial and time-expanded flow-balance constraints conserve fleet units by type, location, and period. Fleet availability requires sum_i NumIdlePlanesInit[v,i] <= a_v. Active-leg demand requires sum_v q_v NumPlanes[v,a] >= P[a]. Route restriction requires NumPlanes[v,a] <= a_v delta[a] for every feasible leg, so inactive feasible legs carry zero assigned fleet units. This is not a VRP: there are no binary route-arc, visit-once, subtour, service-time, load-propagation, or customer-time-window constraints.
natural_language_example: An airline operations team must decide how many aircraft of each fleet type to assign to a small list of active flight legs over several time periods. Each fleet type has a capacity, an operating cost per assigned leg, and a limited number of available aircraft. Passenger demand is specified only for active legs, while inactive feasible legs are explicitly forbidden by the active-leg indicator. Aircraft must be conserved over time: an aircraft can depart a location only if it is initially placed there, has remained idle there, or arrived there from an earlier leg. The goal is to minimize operating cost while satisfying active-leg passenger demand and respecting fleet availability.
